title: feat: initial opendesk Cloudron package with SSO, mail, store metadata and catalog workflow
body:
## Summary

Initial Cloudron package for [opendesk](https://github.com/useopendesk/opendesk) (Apache-2.0), built from source at upstream commit `898e5943a232b72331daeef76678bf9093b9a210`.

- **Cloudron SSO** (`oidc` addon). First sign-in creates the account; password signup stays closed.
- **Platform mail** through the Cloudron relay (`sendmail` addon).
- **Support mailboxes on Cloudron Mail**: the IMAP/SMTP settings fill themselves in, connections use the internal route, and TLS is still verified. In the mailbox dialog, *Email password* is marked **Recommended**. Forwarding is hidden because the package has no inbound SMTP route.
- PostgreSQL addon (`citext`, `vector`), with data in `/app/data`. The realtime gateway runs under supervisord behind nginx.
- Upstream patches live in `patches/0001`–`0004`. Build images are pinned by digest.
- Community-store metadata: icon, five 3:1 store slides made from upstream screenshots (provenance in `DESIGN.md`), and a Cloudron-format `CHANGELOG`.
- A catalog publish workflow that only runs when `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=true` (GHCR image, keyless provenance, `CloudronVersions.json` via the pinned Cloudron CLI 8.2.6), plus a GitHub release workflow.
- Docs: `README.md` (install/setup/config/limits/troubleshooting), `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md`, `docs/PUBLISHING.md`, and a draft forum post in `docs/ANNOUNCEMENT.md`.

## Merge method

**Use a merge commit, not squash.** `iconUrl` and `mediaLinks` in `CloudronManifest.json` point at commits `f6e44e2` and `98b89d4`, and those commits must stay reachable from `main`.

## Verification

- `bash test/package-test.sh`: passed.
- `shellcheck` on `start.sh`, `scripts/*.sh`, `bin/run-realtime`, `bin/opendesk-cli`, `test/package-test.sh`: clean.
- In a scratch copy, `cloudron versions add --state testing` followed by `cloudron versions verify` (CLI 8.2.6): passed.
- Live install updated from this branch with `cloudron update`. `/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/admin/` returned 200, and `/v1/auth/config` reports the Cloudron OIDC provider with `signup_enabled:false`.

## Not yet verified

- Cloudron user sign-in and workspace creation; mailbox receive/reply/alias; backup and restore.
- Catalog install. Publishing needs the repository to be public, plus `CLOUDRON_RELEASE_PAT` and `CLOUDRON_PUBLICATION_ENABLED=true`. Merging does not publish anything.

title: GH#15: chore: release 0.1.3 with the IMAP sync fix
body:
## Summary

Release package 0.1.3 so catalog installs get upstream's fix for IMAP mailboxes that stop syncing after their first pass (forum report: https://forum.cloudron.io/post/131294).

- `CloudronManifest.json`: `version` 0.1.2 → 0.1.3 (the `f9471ba` pin and patches already landed in #14).

## Root cause

In `bb2b56b` (0.1.2), `syncInsertOpts()` in `internal/email/api_mailboxes.go` used `UniqueOpts{ByArgs: true}` with River's default unique states, which include `completed`. A finished `email.sync_mailbox` job blocked every later one-minute `email.sync_due` insert until River pruned it (~24 h). Upstream `9c7cc1a` (#52, included in `f9471ba`) excludes `completed` and adds `ByQueue` so legacy completed rows stop matching immediately on upgrade.

title: GH#12: feat: help centers on custom domains and wildcard subdomains (0.2.0)
body:
## Summary

Help centers on their own domains through Cloudron alias domains, released as package 0.2.0.

- **`CloudronManifest.json`:** `multiDomain: true` lets operators add aliases in the app's *Location*. Version bumped from 0.1.3 to 0.2.0. opendesk stays at `f9471ba`.
- **Exact alias** (for example `help.example.com`): serves the custom domain a brand connects under *Help center → Custom domain*. No package setting is needed. opendesk's DNS check accepts Cloudron's record for the alias, so only the `_opendesk-verify` TXT record is added by hand.
- **Wildcard alias** (for example `*.help.example.com`): `start.sh` sets opendesk's `HELP_DOMAIN` from the only wildcard entry in `CLOUDRON_ALIAS_DOMAINS`, so every brand gets `<slug>.help.example.com`. `HELP_DOMAIN` is now package-owned, so it never names a host Cloudron does not route. It stays unset when there is no wildcard alias, more than one, or a name opendesk would reject. The start log reports which mode is active.
- **Mail is unaffected.** Aliases carry web traffic only. The README says a brand's mailbox usually stays on the main domain, and a domain only needs email enabled in Cloudron for mail addresses on the subdomain itself.
- **Docs:** a README *Help center addresses* section (setup and removal order, DNS records, troubleshooting), `DESCRIPTION.md`, `env.template`, `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md`, and a `docs/PUBLISHING.md` qualification step.

## Fixed along the way: `/help/<slug>` never rendered

`nginx.conf` set `proxy_set_header Connection ""` inside `location /`. nginx then drops every `proxy_set_header` inherited from `server` level, so opendesk received `Host: opendesk` (the upstream name). `helpsite.Middleware` matched no host, and every `/help/<slug>` request in 0.1.x served the web app instead of the help center. All proxy headers now live at server level, and one `map` handles `Connection` for both WebSocket upgrades and keepalive. `test/package-test.sh` now rejects any `proxy_set_header` inside a `location`; it flags all five lines of the old config. Client IPs were not affected: opendesk runs with `TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1` and reads Cloudron's `X-Forwarded-For`.

title: t4: GH#41 GH#45 realtime gateway: clear Hex advisories and bind to loopback (0.2.7)
body:
## Summary

Prepare Cloudron package **0.2.7**, which clears the Hex advisories in the realtime gateway (#41) and binds the gateway to loopback (#45).

Upstream `realtime/mix.lock` still pins `bandit 1.13.1` (12 EEF advisories) and `jose 1.11.12` (8 EEF advisories). That includes upstream `main`, which is 19 commits past our pin, so waiting for an upstream bump isn't an option yet. Upstream `realtime/config/runtime.exs` also hard-codes the gateway to every interface (`ip: {0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}`), so other containers on the Cloudron internal network could reach port 4000 directly, bypassing the internal nginx.

- `patches/0005-realtime-hex-advisories.patch` (new): changes only `realtime/mix.lock`, moving `bandit` to 1.14.1 and `jose` to 1.11.13. These are the versions `mix deps.update bandit jose` picks inside upstream's existing `mix.exs` constraints.
- `patches/0006-realtime-bind-loopback.patch` (new): binds the endpoint to `{127, 0, 0, 1}`, matching the API (`HTTP_ADDR=127.0.0.1:8080`) and NATS (`NATS_LISTEN=127.0.0.1:4222`). The only client is the internal nginx (`upstream realtime { server 127.0.0.1:4000; }`), and clustering is off (`RELEASE_DISTRIBUTION=none`).
- `start.sh`: the gateway comment now names patch 0006 (no behaviour change).
- `CloudronManifest.json`: version 0.2.7. The upstream pin stays at `f38d6f7`.
- `CHANGELOG` / `CHANGELOG.md`: 0.2.7 notes with each advisory classified, plus the loopback bind.
- `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md`: documents patches 0005 and 0006, when to drop them, and how to regenerate 0005.
- `TODO.md`: t4 (#45) entry.

## Advisory classification

| Package | Advisories | Status | Exposure before the fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| bandit | EEF-CVE-2026-111101 (chunked-body amplification), 114216 (chunk-extension smuggling), 113436 (Content-Length/Host bignum parsing) | **fixed** | Reachable, or potentially reachable, through nginx `/socket` over HTTP/1.1 |
| bandit | EEF-CVE-2026-114213 (WebSocket 1-byte continuations), 110314 (frames after server close) | **fixed** | Reachable through `/socket` WebSockets |
| bandit | EEF-CVE-2026-110499, 111103, 115269, 108525, 116078, 109584, 108529 (HTTP/2) | **fixed** | Not reachable from the public domain: the internal nginx speaks HTTP/1.1 to the gateway (`nginx.conf` `proxy_http_version 1.1`). Before 0.2.7 the gateway listened on all interfaces at port 4000, so clients on the Cloudron internal network could reach it directly over cleartext HTTP/2; patch 0006 closes that path. |
| jose | EEF-CVE-2026-65625 … 65632 | **fixed** | Largely unreachable: `Realtime.Auth` only calls `JOSE.JWT.verify_strict(JOSE.JWK.from_oct(secret), ["HS256"], token)`, with no JWE, RSA, ECDSA, X25519 or key export |

Evidence: before the patch, `mix deps.get --only prod` printed `bandit 1.13.1 VULNERABLE!` and `jose 1.11.12 VULNERABLE!` with all 20 IDs. After it, with `bandit 1.14.1` and `jose 1.11.13`, it prints no advisories.

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** High (the gateway's HTTP/WebSocket server, token-verification library and listen address change)
- **Verification:** runtime-verified, at head `aaad7b3`
  - `docker build --target realtime`: all six patches apply cleanly with `git apply --recount` ("Applied patch realtime/mix.lock cleanly", "Applied patch realtime/config/runtime.exs cleanly"), deps compile, and `mix release` succeeds.
  - Loopback smoke test of the built release, run with throwaway secrets. The log shows `Running RealtimeWeb.Endpoint with Bandit 1.14.1 at 127.0.0.1:4000 (http)`.
    - Inside the gateway's network namespace, on `127.0.0.1:4000`: `GET /health` returned `200 ok`. A WebSocket upgrade on `/socket/widget` with an HS256 `widget_ws` token signed independently of JOSE returned `101 Switching Protocols`, and the Phoenix heartbeat replied `phx_reply` `status: ok`. The same upgrade with a forged signature returned `403 Forbidden`, logged as `invalid_token`.
    - From another container on the bridge network, the gateway's IP on port 4000 refused the connection. The same IP from inside the namespace also refused it.
    - `/proc/net/tcp{,6}` lists exactly one listener on port 4000: `127.0.0.1`.
  - Full `docker build .` succeeded. The final image's `realtime/releases/*/runtime.exs` binds `ip: {127, 0, 0, 1}`, and `/app/code/upstream-commit` is `f38d6f70796f1cd5db1f183ff068bb49e7ff9b3b`. The earlier full build at `def4bbf` showed `/app/code/realtime/lib/bandit-1.14.1` and `jose-1.11.13`; patch 0005 is byte-identical since.
  - `bash test/package-test.sh` passed. ShellCheck on `start.sh` was clean, and so was `git diff --check`.
  - `cloudron-package-helper.sh preflight-release v0.2.7` passed at `aaad7b3`. Its only warnings are for the unchanged Go/Node image digest checks, the same as in 0.2.6.
  - There is no Cloudron test app on the configured server, so end-to-end install qualification was not run.
  - Head binding: the final head `1fd5145` differs from `aaad7b3` only in `docs/PACKAGING-NOTES.md` (the layout table and the gateway paragraph now describe the loopback bind) and one `CHANGELOG` line ("patches 0001 to 0004 are unchanged"). `patches/`, `Dockerfile`, `start.sh` and `CloudronManifest.json` are byte-identical. At `1fd5145`, `test/package-test.sh` and `git diff --check` pass.
  - Self-review of the #45 delta: nothing else reaches port 4000. `nginx.conf:51` uses `127.0.0.1:4000`, the Cloudron health check is `/healthz` on `httpPort` 8000 (nginx), there are no `tcpPorts`, and clustering is off.
- **Independent review:** blind acceptance review (fresh context) of the #41 changes found AC1–AC5 satisfied, with no defects, after the first cycle's finding (enumerate every advisory ID) was fixed. `review-evidence-helper.sh blind check-result` reports satisfied (5 of 5 criteria). CodeRabbit's HTTP/2 exposure finding is fixed in `554a014`, and patch 0006 fixes the underlying exposure.

## Decisions

- I used a package-side lock patch because upstream `main` still pins the vulnerable versions. Changing only the lock, not `mix.exs`, keeps the patch minimal. Drop it once upstream's lock carries these versions or newer.
- Patch 0006 hard-codes the loopback address instead of adding an env variable, because every listener in this package is package-owned and upstream has no bind-address setting. Drop it and set the address from `start.sh` if upstream makes it configurable.

Merging and publication happen only after signed maintainer approval of the release issue for the exact final head (`cloudron-release-approval-helper.sh`).
